With vaccinations progressing and policy support in place, the FOMC’s July 28, 2021 decision to keep the federal funds rate at 0–0.25% and continue Treasury and agency MBS purchases remains appropriate for sustaining the recovery and anchoring inflation expectations under average-inflation targeting. Forward guidance and QE at the ZLB help maintain accommodative financial conditions and smooth market functioning.

The Federal Reserve’s Financial Stability Report (May 2021) supports a cautiously positive view but flags vulnerabilities that temper optimism: asset valuations are elevated relative to historical norms; business leverage remains high; and structural funding risks persist in nonbank intermediation (for example, prime money market and open-end bond funds), alongside Treasury market fragilities revealed in past stress. Sectoral risks in commercial real estate—particularly office and lodging—are still notable. Offsetting these risks, bank capital and liquidity are strong, and household balance sheets have generally improved, aided by policy support.

Netting these considerations, the outlook is supportive but measured, with upside from ongoing policy accommodation and growth momentum, and downside from elevated valuations and lingering pandemic-related and market-structure risks.
